articles.title: No meio do campo, a biodiversidade também tem espaço no City Farm | G1
articles.standfirst: Estande de Ciências Biológicas aproxima visitantes da fauna regional e mostra como conhecimento pode contribuir com o campo
articles.summary: Estande de Ciências Biológicas aproxima visitantes da fauna regional e mostra como conhecimento pode contribuir com o campo
articles.body:
Quando se fala em agronegócio, máquinas, lavouras, animais de produção e tecnologia costumam estar entre os primeiros elementos que vêm à cabeça. Mas, no campo, também existe uma diversidade de espécies que participa das relações ecológicas que acontecem diariamente. É justamente esse outro lado da produção que o estande de Ciências Biológicas da FAG pretende apresentar durante a VI edição do City Farm.

Com uma proposta voltada à educação ambiental, a BioFAG levará ao evento animais vivos, exemplares de animais peçonhentos, ossadas e informações sobre a fauna da região. Entre os animais que poderão ser vistos pelo público estão jiboias, iguanas, ouriços e geckos. Também serão apresentados exemplares de cascavel, jararaca, coral, cobra-cipó e diferentes espécies de escorpiões.

Jean Álvaro Fritz Garda, coordenador do curso de Ciências Biológicas do Centro FAG, explica que, mais do que expor os animais, a intenção é utilizá-los como ferramentas para despertar curiosidade e conhecimento. Segundo ele, o contato próximo ajuda a diminuir o medo e a desinformação em relação às espécies.

A experiência também tem uma relação direta com a rotina de quem vive no campo. Animais peçonhentos, por exemplo, podem aparecer em propriedades rurais e, diante de um encontro inesperado, o conhecimento sobre como agir pode fazer diferença.

No estande, a equipe orientará os visitantes sobre as características dos animais e sobre formas adequadas de lidar com essas situações, incluindo a busca por órgãos competentes para o resgate.

Jiboia é uma das espécies que chama a atenção dos visitantes do City Farm. — Foto: Divulgação/Júlia Oliveira Mourão.

Acadêmico do 8º período de Ciências Biológicas e auxiliar de laboratório do Centro FAG, Eduardo Hipólito também participa das atividades de educação ambiental e do cuidado com os animais. Para ele, o contato direto facilita a compreensão sobre características e comportamentos que muitas vezes são desconhecidos pelo público.

“É muito importante esse trabalho que a gente tem no City Farm. Estamos ali para passar o que sabemos dos animais, seja de comportamento, da parte ecológica, a relação que eles têm com o ambiente” , explica Eduardo.

A dinâmica combina a observação dos animais com explicações sobre suas características. Segundo o acadêmico, um exemplar pode ser utilizado para mostrar estruturas específicas e explicar, por exemplo, mecanismos de defesa. Além dos animais vivos, as ossadas também podem ser utilizadas para apresentar características anatômicas das espécies.

“Nos últimos anos, a gente tem percebido que a cada ano aumenta o fluxo de pessoas no estande da Biologia procurando por informações a respeito dos animais e querendo contato mesmo com esses animais e aprender mais sobre eles” , compartilha Jean.

A proposta deste ano ganha ainda mais força com a presença de novos animais e conteúdos. As jiboias maiores, os geckos e outros animais devem chamar a atenção dos visitantes, mas o objetivo permanece sendo o mesmo: transformar a curiosidade em aprendizado.

A BioFAG aproxima os visitantes de diferentes espécies e seus modos de vida. — Foto: Divulgação/Júlia Oliveira Mourão.

A biodiversidade conversa com a produção

Para além da aproximação com os animais, a equipe da BioFAG pretende apresentar, durante o City Farm, resultados de uma pesquisa realizada desde o início do ano em um fragmento de mata localizado próximo a uma área de produção da FAG.

O trabalho acompanha a biodiversidade presente no local e busca observar como as mudanças sazonais e as alterações nas culturas agrícolas influenciam o comportamento e a presença de diferentes espécies. A ideia central é levar ao público um retrato da biodiversidade encontrada na região e mostrar as relações que existem entre áreas de produção e ambientes naturais.

Para o coordenador do curso, compreender essas relações é importante porque a área produtiva também é um ambiente onde diferentes interações ecológicas acontecem. Algumas delas podem, inclusive, beneficiar a própria produção. Entre os exemplos estão os animais que atuam como polinizadores, dispersores de sementes e controladores naturais de determinadas pragas.

Na prática, a presença de áreas de mata próximas às lavouras pode oferecer abrigo, água e condições para a reprodução de espécies que também participam dessas relações. Com isso, alguns animais podem contribuir para o controle natural de organismos que afetam as plantações.

É uma perspectiva que aproxima a Biologia de uma discussão cada vez mais presente no próprio setor produtivo: como utilizar o conhecimento sobre os ecossistemas para tornar os processos agrícolas mais eficientes e sustentáveis.

Gato-maracajá encontrado no corredor ecológico da Fazenda Escola do Centro FAG. — Foto: Divulgação/Ciências Biológicas FAG.

Bioinsumo: um aliado da sustentabilidade

Outro tema que estará presente no estande é o uso de bioinsumos. O curso de Ciências Biológicas tem acadêmicos realizando estágios e atividades nessa área, inclusive relacionados à produção de alternativas biológicas para o manejo de pragas.

A proposta da BioFAG é apresentar ao público como o conhecimento biológico pode contribuir para novas estratégias de manejo e para o desenvolvimento de soluções que dialoguem com as necessidades do setor.

Para Eduardo, levar esse tipo de conhecimento ao público do City Farm também pode ampliar a aproximação entre a Biologia e o agronegócio. Segundo ele, essa aproximação pode ocorrer não apenas na educação ambiental, mas também em questões relacionadas à convivência entre produtores e biodiversidade e ao uso de alternativas como os bioinsumos.

Assim, o estande de Ciências Biológicas amplia a experiência do City Farm ao trazer para perto do público animais que despertam curiosidade e, ao mesmo tempo, apresentar informações sobre o papel que diferentes espécies desempenham nos ambientes naturais e nas áreas de produção.

A expectativa é que o visitante saia do estande conhecendo melhor a fauna regional e percebendo que, no campo, produção e biodiversidade estão inseridas em um mesmo ambiente e podem ser compreendidas a partir do conhecimento científico.

A VI edição do City Farm FAG será realizada de 26 a 29 de novembro, no Centro FAG, em Cascavel. O evento reunirá empresas, produtores, profissionais, acadêmicos e visitantes em uma programação voltada ao agronegócio, à tecnologia, à inovação e ao conhecimento.

Acesse o site e o Instagram do City Farm FAG para ficar por dentro de todas as informações do evento.

articles.title: Onda de furtos na avenida em Belém preocupa moradores | G1
articles.standfirst: Câmeras de segurança registraram ações de criminosos que levam fiação elétrica, invadem casas e furtam até caixas d'água à luz do dia. Prejuízos passam de R$ 3 mil.
articles.summary: Câmeras de segurança registraram ações de criminosos que levam fiação elétrica, invadem casas e furtam até caixas d'água à luz do dia. Prejuízos passam de R$ 3 mil.
articles.body:
Uma sequência de furtos e invasões tem tirado o sossego de quem mora ou trabalha em um trecho da Avenida Conselheiro Furtado, no bairro da Cremação, em Belém .

Os crimes, que acontecem inclusive à luz do dia, têm como alvo desde fiação elétrica e de telefonia até objetos de estabelecimentos comerciais.

Imagens de câmeras de monitoramento flagraram diversas dessas ações criminosas, que mostram a audácia dos suspeitos circulando livremente pela área.

A sensação de insegurança afeta quem acabou de se mudar para o bairro. É o caso de um morador que comprou uma casa recentemente na avenida. Após passar por reformas, a família se mudou há menos de três meses, mas o curto período já foi suficiente para registrar o primeiro prejuízo.

"Nós estamos vivendo com medo, não dá para ficar assim", relatou o proprietário, que preferiu não se identificar.

O imóvel foi alvo de criminosos que violaram o cadeado do portão. Câmeras de segurança registraram a movimentação de um suspeito que, segundo denúncias de vizinhos, monitora a rotina das residências antes de agir.

Após a invasão, os proprietários precisaram reforçar as portas e refazer toda a instalação elétrica que havia sido levada.

O problema não é isolado. Outros moradores da Conselheiro Furtado relatam prejuízos semelhantes com o furto de cabos de cobre. Em apenas uma das ocorrências na vizinhança, o custo para repor a fiação furtada chegou a cerca de R$ 3 mil.

Além das residências, os pequenos comércios da Cremação também entraram na mira dos criminosos. Em um ponto comercial da avenida, duas caixas d'água foram furtadas .

O circuito de segurança do local registrou a ação inusitada: um homem chega a pé, se abaixa, pega os dois reservatórios e vai embora caminhando tranquilamente pela via pública.

O comerciante Mauro Aguiar do Amaral conta que só percebeu o crime quando precisou usar a água.

"Eu fui tomar banho e cadê? Não achei a caixa. Quando fui olhar, tinham levado", lamenta o comerciante.

De acordo com a vizinhança, o homem que aparece nas imagens das caixas d'água é o mesmo suspeito visto rondando a área em outras ocasiões para cometer pequenos delitos.

Este não é o primeiro alerta de segurança emitido por moradores da Cremação neste mês. Reportagens recentes já haviam mostrado o avanço dos furtos de fiação e invasões a domicílios no bairro, evidenciando uma rotina de medo para quem precisa transitar ou trabalhar na região.

Os moradores cobram um posicionamento das autoridades e o reforço no policiamento ostensivo no bairro para coibir a ação dos assaltantes.

"Se a gente não tiver uma segurança, fica difícil para as pessoas trabalharem e viverem em paz", desabafa outro morador da área.

articles.title: Veja a entrevista de Professor Túlio Lopes no MG1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PCB ao governo de Minas concedeu entrevista ao MG1.
articles.summary: Candidato do PCB ao governo de Minas concedeu entrevista ao MG1.
articles.body:
O candidato do PCB ao governo de Minas Gerais, Professor Túlio Lopes, afirmou, em entrevista ao MG1 desta sexta-feira (25), que pretende ampliar a participação da população em decisões do estado por meio de conselhos populares.

Lopes também defendeu mudanças no modelo atual de segurança pública e a valorização dos servidores estaduais.

Além das sabatinas de 30 minutos com os seis nomes mais bem colocados na pesquisa Datafolha de 11 de setembro, exibidas ao vivo na semana passada , a Globo convidou os outros cinco concorrentes para entrevistas gravadas. As respostas somadas de cada entrevistado têm dois minutos.

A ordem das entrevistas foi definida por sorteio: na segunda-feira (21), foi a vez de Ben Mendes (Missão) ; na terça (22), de Rafael Duda (PSTU) ; na quarta (23), de Indira Xavier (UP) ; e na quinta (24), de Henrique Áreas (PCO).

Veja o que Professor Túlio Lopes falou sobre os seguintes temas:

Questionado sobre a proposta de criar conselhos populares para acompanhar ações do governo e fiscalizar contratos, Professor Túlio Lopes afirmou que pretende ampliar a participação da população em instâncias de decisão do estado.

Segundo o candidato, a proposta inclui a democratização de conselhos já existentes e a criação de novos espaços de representação regional e setorial.

Túlio também defendeu a participação de sindicatos, especialistas, intelectuais e trabalhadores na formulação e acompanhamento de políticas públicas.

"Nós defendemos, primeiro, a democratização dos conselhos já existentes, como os conselhos estaduais de Saúde, Educação e Meio Ambiente. [...] Queremos criar instâncias de participação efetiva, garantindo uma democracia substantiva para o povo trabalhador mineiro."

Ao comentar a proposta de desmilitarização e unificação das forças de segurança, Professor Túlio Lopes afirmou que o modelo atual não tem sido capaz de responder aos problemas da área e defendeu a construção de um novo sistema de segurança pública.

Conforme o candidato, a proposta passa pela valorização dos profissionais do setor e pela reformulação da formação oferecida aos agentes.

"Nós, junto com o Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública, queremos pensar um novo modelo de segurança pública, porque o modelo existente não está funcionando definitivamente."

Túlio afirmou ainda que a mudança busca evitar a criminalização de movimentos sociais e garantir a segurança pública como um direito da população.

Questionado sobre propostas de valorização dos servidores estaduais, incluindo concursos públicos, recomposição salarial e redução da jornada de trabalho sem redução de salários, Professor Túlio Lopes afirmou que pretende ampliar os investimentos nos serviços públicos.

O candidato disse que os recursos para essas medidas viriam do fim de benefícios fiscais concedidos pelo estado e do aumento da arrecadação.

"Nós iremos garantir todos os recursos necessários para o fortalecimento do setor público e a valorização dos servidores."

Professor Túlio Lopes também destacou sua trajetória como servidor público e afirmou ter assumido compromissos com entidades representativas da categoria.

articles.title: Special agents blood and urine test results stolen in FBI hack
articles.summary: Experts say the hack could leave agents vulnerable to scams, blackmail and targeted attacks.
articles.body:
Cyber-criminals who hacked the FBI say they have extremely sensitive medical data for thousands of its special agents.

BBC News has seen samples of the stolen "fitness-for-work" medical examinations, which contain information such as blood and urine test results, and doctors' notes mentioning conditions such as a "shellfish and banana allergy".

The records include agents' full names and addresses, as well as references to medical concerns including 'blood in the urine' and 'high cholesterol'.

Experts say the hack - which the FBI is investigating - could leave agents vulnerable to scams, blackmail and targeted attacks, as well as help criminals impersonate law enforcement officers.

"The list maps thousands of agents against their medical and fitness records," said Etay Maor, vice-president of threat intelligence at Cato Networks.

"Passwords can be reset if stolen, but medical records cannot, so once this data is out, it stays compromised for good. That permanence, applied across an entire workforce, is what makes this leak so serious."

The FBI has not responded to requests for comment. However, on Wednesday it acknowledged the breach and said it was "aggressively investigating" how it happened.

The cyber-criminal group ShinyHunters claims it breached FBI systems on Monday, and later posted details of the attack on its darknet site.

The group also shared samples of the alleged stolen data with reporters, along with an extortion demand.

Unusually, the hackers are not demanding money. Instead, they are seeking a retraction of an FBI advisory published in May, which they claim "offended" them.

The samples shared with journalists appear genuine and include names, addresses, phone numbers, badge numbers, job titles and information about spouses.

The records appear to relate to thousands of agents, including senior officials such as deputy directors.

Professor Ciaran Martin, the former head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, has described the hack - if confirmed - "as serious as it gets when it comes to data breaches."

'Phishing, impersonation, identity fraud'

The news agency Reuters reports that some of the data includes information on agents involved in investigations relating to Russia, China and drug cartels.

Reporting by 404 Media suggests details of a previously little-known FBI hacking unit may also have been exposed .

It was initially thought the breach affected the FBI's 38,000 current employees, but the hackers now claim the number could be far higher.

The group says it underestimated the scale of the data theft and now claims to hold sensitive information on around 60,000 current and former FBI staff.

Jamie Akhtar, chief executive and co-founder of CyberSmart, said the hackers' claims should be treated with caution but that the breach appeared to be extremely concerning.

"Such data could be used for highly convincing phishing, impersonation, identity fraud, blackmail or even operations targeting law-enforcement personnel, making the potential implications particularly serious," he said.

The hackers, who communicate with reporters in English via the messaging service, Telegram, say they will publish the full dataset in five days unless the FBI meets their demands.

ShinyHunters is an international hacking collective that has been active since 2019 and has been linked to a number of high-profile cyber-attacks, including incidents affecting Rockstar Games and the education platform Canvas .

The group claims it exploited a vulnerability in an Oracle cloud storage system used by the FBI, gaining access to multiple platforms including FBIJobs, FBI BEAST, which handles background checks on employees and applicants, FBI MedLink, which stores medical records, and FBI BICS, which contains investigative information.

In a statement posted on X, the FBI said it was still trying to determine whether the hackers had breached its systems directly or compromised a third-party provider.

"We are actively and aggressively investigating this matter and working closely with those third-party providers that support FBIJobs.gov to mitigate any and all risk," the statement said.

articles.title: Peshawar seeks revival of Dilip Kumar’s ancestral home as heritage landmark
articles.summary: AMRITSAR: With the ancestral home of legendary actor Dilip Kumar in Peshawar in restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) province of Pakistan reportedly reduced
articles.body: AMRITSAR: With the ancestral home of legendary actor Dilip Kumar in Peshawar in restive Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KPK) province of Pakistan reportedly reduced to a fragile remnant of its past, the Saragarhi Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee has urged the KPK government to immediately undertake its restoration and preserve the birthplace of one of the subcontinent’s most celebrated cinematic icons.Sunny Singh, president of the committee, visited the historic house in Mohalla Khudadad near Qissa Khwani Bazaar and expressed concern over its deteriorating condition. The century-old house, where Dilip Kumar was born as Muhammad Yusuf Khan on December 11, 1922, has long been regarded as an important link to the actor’s early life and Peshawar’s cultural history.“I had the opportunity to visit the historic ancestral home of the legendary subcontinental actor Dilip Kumar in Peshawar. Standing at this historic site and feeling the moments of the past was a unique and memorable experience,” he said.He said Dilip Kumar was not merely a towering name in the film industry but also a source of pride for Peshawar, making his ancestral home an important part of the region’s shared cultural heritage.Singh said a large number of Dilip Kumar’s admirers continue to visit the property but return disappointed after seeing its condition. He said following his visit, he held discussions with members of the gurdwara management and local social activists and decided to approach the KPK chief minister for immediate restoration of the ancestral house of Dilip Kumar.Notably, Sunny Singh, president of the Saragarhi Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, regularly observes the anniversary of the Battle of Saragarhi and pays tribute to the 21 Sikh soldiers who laid down their lives fighting bravely against overwhelming odds. He has remained committed to preserving the memory and legacy of these brave soldiers.Being a social activist also, I have decided with my team to observe the birth and death anniversary of Dilip Kumar at his house.The committee wants the restoration work to begin at the earliest and be completed before the actor’s birth anniversary on December 11.According to reports, the house was declared a national heritage site in July 2014 and was subsequently notified as a protected monument under the Antiquities Act. The government had also proposed acquiring the property and converting it into a museum depicting Dilip Kumar’s journey from Peshawar to Mumbai.However, despite repeated plans for preservation, the property has continued to deteriorate. A report in June 2025 said the upper portion of the ancestral house had collapsed, leaving only parts of the original structure intact.Dilip Kumar had retained an emotional connection with Peshawar and his childhood home. During a visit to the city, he reportedly visited the house and expressed his affection for the place associated with his early years.Singh said preserving the property would allow future generations to remain connected with the shared history and cultural heritage associated with Dilip Kumar and Peshawar.“The historic places of our past should be preserved so that future generations can also remain connected with their cultural heritage,” he said.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: China's coal mines generate billions of cubic metres of water; researchers say it could help cool data centres
articles.summary: China's coal mines generate billions of cubic metres of water each year, and researchers say much of that resource could potentially be redirected toward
articles.body: China's coal mines generate billions of cubic metres of water each year, and researchers say much of that resource could potentially be redirected toward cooling the country's rapidly expanding data-centre infrastructure. In a review published in the Journal of Environmental Chemical Engineering titled The feasibility and prospects of coal mine water as a cooling medium for data centers, researchers led by Zaining Li assessed whether treated coal mine water could replace municipal make-up water in liquid-cooled data centres. They estimate that China's data centres could consume more than 3 billion cubic metres of water annually by 2030, while coal mine water generation could reach an estimated 12.96 billion cubic metres that year. The authors conclude that, after appropriate treatment, the resource has sufficient quantity and potentially suitable quality for data-centre cooling, although they identify pilot-scale implementation as the next step.Data centres could more than double their water demand by 2030The review estimates that China's data-centre water consumption will increase from approximately 1.3 billion cubic metres in 2024 to more than 3 billion cubic metres in 2030. The researchers link the increase to expanding cloud computing, high-performance computing and artificial intelligence infrastructure. More efficient liquid-cooling technologies can help reduce energy consumption and bring power usage effectiveness, or PUE, below 1.2, but the cooling systems can still require high-quality make-up water. The authors therefore examine coal mine water as one of several alternative sources that could reduce pressure on conventional freshwater supplies. As an indication of the industry's existing scale, the review cites Alibaba's fiscal 2024 disclosure of 0.036 billion cubic metres of water consumption.Coal mining produces a huge but underused water streamThe opportunity exists partly because China's enormous coal industry produces substantial quantities of mine water alongside the coal itself. The review notes that China produced 4.7 billion tonnes of raw coal in 2023 and estimates that approximately two tonnes of water are generated for every tonne of coal mined. That corresponds to roughly 9.4 billion cubic metres of coal mine water in 2023. The researchers describe the water as potentially attractive for cooling because underground mine water can have relatively low and stable temperatures. But untreated mine water is not automatically suitable for a data centre: its mineral composition can promote calcium carbonate scaling, corrosion and biofouling, creating risks for cooling equipment.Treatment is essential before the water reaches cooling systemsThe review therefore focuses heavily on how coal mine water could be treated to meet the quality requirements of liquid-cooling systems. Water chemistry varies between mining regions, so the researchers examine contaminants and characteristics including ammonia nitrogen, calcium hardness, chloride ions, turbidity, suspended solids and total hardness. They compare conventional multi-stage treatment approaches with an integrated electrochemical “short-flow” process and discuss technologies including oxidation, chemical flocculation, membrane separation, electrochemical treatment and biofiltration. The authors conclude that advanced treatment can bring coal mine water into compliance with cooling-water requirements, but they also stress that treatment has to be optimised for local water chemistry, operating conditions, energy use and seasonal variation.The researchers estimate that treated mine water could be cheaperThe review's economic analysis estimates a treatment cost of approximately 1.37 yuan per cubic metre for coal mine water, compared with 3.87 yuan per cubic metre for municipal water. On the assumptions used in the analysis, the additional treatment infrastructure could have an estimated payback period of 4.6 to 8.8 years. The paper also models environmental benefits under a broader scenario in which data centres improve PUE from 1.6 to 1.2 while integrating regional wind power, estimating a 93.8% reduction in annual carbon emissions. That figure should not be interpreted as the carbon reduction produced by substituting coal mine water alone, because the model combines several changes to the data centre's energy and cooling system.The proposal still needs to move from modelling to pilot projectsThe researchers ultimately present coal mine water as a potential circular resource for China's data-centre industry rather than a technology that has already been commercially proven at scale. Their review provides a framework for assessing water availability, treatment requirements, operating risks, economics and environmental effects, and they propose pilot implementations to test the approach under real operating conditions. The paper also points to China's existing water-conservation and circular-economy policies, including the Water Ten Plan and measures associated with the 14th Five-Year Plan, as potential policy support for wider adoption. Although the analysis focuses on Chinese coal mines and data centres, the authors say the methods for assessing water quality, optimising treatment and managing risks could also be applied to other unconventional water sources internationally.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sikh woman in Canada killed at home; neighbors saw her mother frantically running out with grandkids
articles.summary: A violent crime took place at a Sikh household in Ontario's London neighborhood which the police characterized as femicide resulting from an intimate
articles.body: A violent crime took place at a Sikh household in Ontario's London neighborhood which the police characterized as femicide resulting from an intimate partner violence incident. The incident took place on September 15 at a home on Chelton Road in the Summerside neighborhood. When officers arrived at the scene, they found Raman Devi, a mother of two, suffering from life-threatening injuries. She was taken to the hospital, where she later died. Police have charged 41-year-old Mandee Singh, her husband, with second-degree murder.Shocking details revealed by neighborsNeighbors told CBC News that they saw Raman Devi's mother frantically exiting the house with the children before police arrived. "We saw an old lady coming out shouting and hitting herself, with two [children]," said Sam Awdi, who lives across the street. "I feel bad. I've been in this city 40 years but never saw something like that, honestly," he said.Raman Devi was taking a massage therapy program and the incident shook her mates, the London Free Press reported.Sandra Sanchez, one of Devi’s classmates, launched an online fundraiser. “Her presence brought love and joy to those around her, and she will forever hold a special place in our hearts,” Sanchez wrote. “Above all, she was a loving mother, her children were her world, and her family meant everything to her. Losing a mother is an unimaginable loss, especially for her children, who now have to face a future without her by their side.”Gurdwara London Sikh Society too set up a fundraiser for Devi. "The loss of a mother is an unimaginable pain. For Raman Devi's young children, this loss is especially heartbreaking, as they must now face the years ahead without their mother’s love, care, guidance, and comforting presence. No child should have to experience such a profound loss at such a young age," their fundraiser said.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pakistan govt crackdown forces PTI retreat? Imran's party likely to postpone Sept 27 Islamabad march
articles.summary: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4, party insiders said on Friday.
articles.body: The Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) has decided to postpone its planned march to Islamabad from September 27 to October 4, party insiders said on Friday.The PTI had planned the march to the capital to demand the release of its incarcerated founder and former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. The decision to delay the protest apparently came in response to the tough measures taken by the federal government to prevent it.According to PTI sources, the decision was taken at a party meeting and will be formally announced by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister and PTI leader Sohail Afridi.Earlier in the day, Afridi had asserted at a press conference in Peshawar that the planned long march would go ahead despite road blockades and other measures. However, he expressed concern over reports of nails being driven into roads at the provincial boundaries, questioning whether a conspiracy to “cut” Khyber Pakhtunkhwa off from the rest of Pakistan had formally begun.“Our long march will definitely take place. This time, we will definitely come out. Put nails on the roads, place containers or fire bullets, we will come out. We will end this corrupt system of fake rulers,” he told reporters.“Pakistan will not break at any cost and we will save Pakistan,” he added.Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been held at Rawalpindi’s high-security Adiala Jail since 2023, when he was arrested following his conviction in a corruption case.Pakistan minister says PTI has 'run away'Pakistan information minister Ataullah Tarar reacted to the reports by saying the PTI had “run away” because it had made “no preparations” for the march to Islamabad.“There are no preparations for the PTI’s long march either, and that is why they have backed out of this protest. If they have the courage, let them come and hold the march,” Tarar said.The federal government had placed shipping containers along Islamabad’s main roads, allowing them to be closed at short notice ahead of the planned march.Hotels in the Faizabad area of Rawalpindi had been closed, while restaurants and shopkeepers were directed to shut their businesses. Guest houses and transport terminals in Faizabad had also been ordered to close from Friday night.Thousands of security personnel were deployed in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, the capital’s twin city and home to Pakistan Army headquarters, to control Khan’s supporters.Tensions over the planned protest continued despite PTI chairman Gohar Ali Khan urging the government to open negotiations and warning against confronting political workers with force.(With PTI inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: Satya Niketan collapse: Delhi govt forms high-powered panel to examine student accommodation, frame PG rules
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has constituted a high-powered committee to examine student accommodation and safety in the capital and recommend
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has constituted a high-powered committee to examine student accommodation and safety in the capital and recommend time-bound measures, the Delhi high court was informed on Friday during a hearing on the September 6 Satya Niketan building collapse.The committee has already decided to prepare a regulatory framework for paying guest (PG) accommodation and private student hostels in Delhi.The submission was made during the hearing of a matter concerning the building collapse in Satya Niketan, where a boys' paying-guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus had collapsed while repair work was underway, killing seven people, including five students, and injuring several others.A bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia was informed by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) that immediately after the September 6 incident, the matter was taken up at the highest executive level of the civic body.The MCD also informed the court that five officers across the entire supervisory chain of the corporation, including a deputy commissioner, had been suspended.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, representing the Delhi government, MCD and Delhi Police, gave details of other steps taken by the authorities.The court also termed Delhi University's affidavit "absolutely vague". The varsity's counsel assured the court that a better response would be filed.According to the MCD's affidavit, the Delhi government constituted a magisterial inquiry into the collapse to examine issues including the validity of permissions, compliance with building bye-laws and the role of the concerned officials.The MCD said no sanctioned building plan had been approved for the property and that it had not been constructed pursuant to valid MCD permission.The civic body also said a time-bound survey and inspection of PG buildings identified across all 12 zones under its jurisdiction had been undertaken.Of 2,453 PG buildings surveyed, 2,342 were found to be visibly safe, 91 required minor repairs, 30 required major repairs and four were found to be in dangerous condition."In addition to that, eight load-bearing structures above ground-plus three storeys and 77 framed structures above ground-plus four storeys are being separately identified for close monitoring as the same may be vulnerable," it said.Cases involving any prima facie issue concerning immediate structural safety or danger to life are being prioritised for appropriate inspection and strict action in accordance with law, the MCD said in its affidavit.The Delhi government's High-Powered Committee on student accommodation and safety was constituted through a September 10 order to examine issues relating to student accommodation and safety in Delhi and recommend appropriate, time-bound measures."In its meeting held on September 15, the committee, among other decisions, resolved to prepare a regulatory framework for paying guest accommodations and private student hostels.It was decided that the Department of Training and Technical Education (DTTE) and the Department of Higher Education (DHE) shall jointly prepare a regulatory framework for PG accommodation and private student hostels," it said.The committee also decided that the framework would be developed in consultation with the stakeholder agency or department and should take into account the experience of other states and Union Territories in regulating PG accommodations.The Delhi Police, in its reply, said six accused, including the owners of the collapsed Satya Niketan building, had failed to take adequate safety precautions during construction or repair work, creating a situation that endangered human lives and ultimately caused deaths.It said the building collapsed due to excessive structural load or weakening of the existing structure, endangering human life and resulting in casualties.The MCD affidavit was filed in a pending PIL by law student Aniket Kumar Gupta, seeking urgent medical care and rehabilitation of affected students, Rs 1 crore compensation for the families of the deceased and preservation of crucial evidence relating to the collapse.The court permitted retired IPS officer Kiran Bedi to address it in the matter and asked the parties to also supply her with the documents they would place on record.The court listed the matter for further hearing on October 14 and said that if the Delhi government's High-Powered Committee meeting takes place in the meantime, its minutes should be placed on record.On September 7, the high court had ordered a high-level MCD inquiry into the building collapse and made it clear that the government could not evade responsibility.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also articles.title: Ed Sheeran concerts cancelled becuase of bad weather
articles.summary: The star's concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday are cancelled after  severe weather warnings.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran's concerts in Massachusetts on Friday and Saturday have been cancelled because of severe weather warnings in the area.

The singer had been scheduled to perform two shows at the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, near Boston, as part of his current US tour.

The tour has been in the headlines because of a row over a decision to drop Sheeran's support act Macklemore for making pro-Palestinian comments on stage. Stadium owners including the Gillette Stadium's Robert Kraft lobbied for his removal.

A statement from the venue said: "Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, the promoter and tour have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium."

It added: "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority.

"Refunds are available now at the point of purchase. Ticketholders who purchased through Ticketmaster will be automatically refunded."

Weather warnings for high winds are in force in the area until the early hours of Sunday, and officials have told drivers to minimise travel.

Sheeran was at the eye of a very different storm last week after the decision to drop Macklemore from his tour.

The decision came after the rapper made on-stage comments at earlier concerts including calling for "free Palestine" and referring to "genocide" in Gaza, as well as showing images of Gaza.

Kraft, who is Jewish, accused the US rapper of hate speech and said Macklemore would not be allowed to appear at the Gillette Stadium, the home of his New England Patriots American football team.

Sheeran said the decision to drop Macklemore was made by his promoter, not by him. The promoter said venue owners including Kraft would have refused to let the concerts take place if Macklemore was on the bill.

Macklemore's removal from the tour led Sheeran's other support and backing artists to pull out in protest, and sparked a heated debate over free speech and the role of politics in music.

Returning to the stage last weekend, Sheeran told fans he "had to take and make difficult decisions - and I am making mistakes - and I'm so, so sorry".

articles.title: 2027 UP assembly polls: Fight against BJP or Congress? Why Akhilesh’s ‘rath’ show in Raebareli is message for Rahul
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Is Uttar Pradesh all set to go the Bihar way for the opposition’s INDIA bloc? Wait, we are not talking about the results yet.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Is Uttar Pradesh all set to go the Bihar way for the opposition’s INDIA bloc? Wait, we are not talking about the results yet. This is about the all-too-familiar alliance strains between INDIA bloc allies - the Samajwadi Party and the Congress in the run-up to UP assembly elections early next year.On Thursday, Akhilesh Yadav unveiled the Samajwadi Party's 'PDA Rath' which he will use for a statewide campaign in the run-up to the 2027 assembly poll. While his fight is against the BJP, the first stop of his rath was Raebareli - a Congress bastion represented by the Gandhis for decades.Also, while Akhilesh targeted the BJP, he had a clear message for the Congress also.“Alliance will happen. We will also go with the alliance. Winnability will be the criteria for deciding seats. For us, it is not about seats, it is about victory. Whosoever can win can take the seat.”The BJP was quick to take digs at both allies and suggested that now Congress should start its campaign from Yadav bastion Mainpuri.This was not an isolated remark. The SP and the Congress have been engaged in a war of words over seat sharing for quite some time now. The open fight has an uncanny resemblance to how events had unfolded between the INDIA bloc allies in Bihar.INDIA bloc's failed Bihar experimentCut to the 2025 Bihar assembly elections.INDIA bloc allies - the RJD and the Congress engaged in a continuous war of words in Bihar over seat-sharing and CM face, while the BJP-led NDA managed a smooth division of seats. What started as public posturing between INDIA bloc allies ended up in public sparring between them as the divided opposition alliance was decimated in the polls.The two parties campaigned separately for most of the time as they could not agree on seat sharing. They took out separate yatras across the state. While Rahul Gandhi undertook the “Vote Adhikar Yatra,” RJD’s Tejashwi Yadav went across the state with his “Bihar Adhikar Yatra.” Ironically, it was the success of the two yatras that boomeranged on the alliance as it made seat-sharing bitter and difficult.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();In the run-up to the Bihar elections, Tejashwi Yadav was confident of a sweep. The Congress was also not willing to budge, guided by its improved showing in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in the state. The two parties used pressure tactics against each other. So much so that the INDIA bloc went into the elections as a divided house despite last-minute agreements and adjustments to keep the alliance intact.Uttar Pradesh appears to be headed the same way, at least as of now. We have already seen a lot of public posturing and sparring between the leaders of the INDIA bloc partners. Both the Congress and the SP have repeatedly claimed that the opposition’s fight against the BJP can be led only by their respective leaders.The SP and Congress contested the 2024 Lok Sabha polls together in Uttar Pradesh and won 43 seats between them, with the SP winning 37 and the Congress six. The alliance also won the Faizabad seat, which includes Ayodhya, where the BJP won in 2019.And that is perhaps where lies the genesis of this power tussle. Both the SP and the Congress feel that it was their party and leader who played a greater role in the 2024 electoral success and hence want the advantage to flow accordingly in seat sharing for the assembly elections.Rahul or Akhilesh vs BJPOne look at the latest broadside between the two parties and we know why seat sharing between them may not be smooth.Recently, Samajwadi Party MP from Kairana Iqra Hasan and Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood, both elected in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as part of the SP-Congress alliance, publicly pitched their respective party leaders to take on the BJP."Only Rahul Gandhi is the opposition voice across the country, which unnerves the BJP. Rahul ji has done the hard work and created a favourable atmosphere. So make no mistake, nothing is possible without Rahul ji, and no one should have any doubts about this," Masood said.Days later, Hasan responded and pitched SP chief Yadav as the key to the alliance's prospects.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();"Only Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. On its own, the Congress won't be able to achieve much," she said.Last week, Congress Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam signalled a firm stance regarding upcoming electoral negotiations and said that any seat-sharing arrangement with the Samajwadi Party (SP) must be built on mutual respect and equal standing.Clarifying reports regarding seat distribution, Gautam claimed that formal discussions with the SP have not yet begun. While expressing open flexibility for minor adjustments, he stressed that the Congress would not compromise its organisational self-respect or dignity in any prospective deal."We have made one thing very clear. The Congress is the country's oldest party. It was the Congress that led the freedom struggle. Any alliance formed will be based on mutual respect; there will be equal partnership and dignity. Sure, we can show some flexibility; there might be minor adjustments, but we cannot compromise on our dignity," the Congress leader said.The contrasting assertions come despite messages of unity from both sides of the divide. Akhilesh is riding high on SP’s Lok Sabha success in Uttar Pradesh. The Congress, which is trying hard to revive its lost electoral fortunes, does not want to compromise on its expansion plans in one of the most politically important states.The Owaisi factorThe problem is that both the parties are wooing the same social base in the state - minorities, Dalits, women, youth. Akhilesh is missing no opportunity to expand his PDA’s - Pichda Dalit and Alpsankhyak - base by making concerted attempts to include Pandits, Aadhi aabadi (women) and other social groups. The Congress is also wooing the Brahmins, the Dalits and the women in a big way.What the two bickering allies don't realise that there are several other parties who are also reaching out to the same social base. For instance, Mayawati and Chandrashekhar Azad are also going all out to woo Dalits. Then there is Owaisi, who has already put both the parties in a Catch22 situation by offering them an alliance against the BJP. Owaisi's proposal is like a double-edged sword for the two parties. If they accept his offer, the BJP will gun for them. If they reject the offer, Owaisi will use the rejection to rally the Muslims against them.Lok Sabha gains, assembly painsThe Samjawadi Party and the Congress may do well to learn lessons from the Bihar debacle before it’s too late. Lok Sabha elections and assembly elections are two very different games and success in one does not automatically translate into success in another. There are numerous instances to show that alliances which did well in Lok Sabha elections failed in assembly elections. Maharashtra is a case in point. The Maha Vikas Aghadi of the opposition parties - Congress, Shiv Sena and the NCP did very well in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, putting the BJP on the backfoot. But a year later in 2025 - the opposition alliance was decimated by the BJP in the assembly elections. So, Akhilesh and Rahul need to decide if they want to keep on flexing muscles at each other or unite in time to pose a challenge to the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Unease within NDA over EC-SIR row? Three BJP allies seek poll body clarification as opposition keeps up pressure
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Unease within the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over a media report concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Unease within the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over a media report concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar surfaced on Friday, with three BJP allies urging the Election Commission of India (ECI) to issue a clearer response.Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) president Chirag Paswan was the first NDA ally to urge the ECI to dispel “misgivings in the minds of the people.”“Let me make it clear that, as part of the government, I do not intend to defend what is a constitutional body. I am also not much worried about the allegations made by the opposition, which will always take a stand that suits it politically,” Paswan told reporters in Patna.“However, if people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy. Therefore, I think the Election Commission must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying, but it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people,” the Hajipur MP added.Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) chief and Rajya Sabha MP Upendra Kushwaha also called for a clarification, saying the controversy had created “confusion” among the public."The controversy regarding the SIR has created a situation of significant confusion among the public. The matter needs to be addressed. The Election Commission should immediately issue a clarification regarding the actual situation to clear up this confusion," Kushwaha posted on X.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) described the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Andhra Pradesh as a “success,” while noting that a clarification from the ECI would be “beneficial”.“The exercise has been a success. Even the opposition has not been able to substantiate its concerns regarding the process in Andhra Pradesh. At the same time, the Election Commission of India is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution,” TDP MP Lavu Srikrishna Devarayalu said.What is the controversyThe allies’ remarks came after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had, on at least 14 occasions over the past 10 months, recorded objections to decisions and orders apparently issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The objections reportedly related to changes to the statutory voter registration Form 6, the process for adding and deleting names from electoral rolls, and the centralised control of the electoral roll database.The report prompted opposition parties to demand the CEC’s removal and call for the SIR exercise to be halted.The ECI, however, asserted that differences of opinion among its members were a “normal part of deliberation” and maintained that its final decisions, including those concerning the SIR, had been “unanimous”.According to the Commission, all its official orders and directions had legal sanction, while describing the suggestions made by the two Election Commissioners as efforts to improve electoral processes. Neither Sandhu nor Joshi has publicly commented on the objections attributed to them.The BJP, meanwhile, has played down the reported differences within the Commission, saying that the exchange of views during official deliberations reflected “pure democracy." The saffron party's West Bengal unit chief, Samik Bhattacharya, for instance, suggested that Gyanesh Kumar be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the country's third-highest civilan honour."The fact is, even the Congress party itself doesn't heed Rahul Gandhi's words; they don't take him seriously... Gyanesh Kumar deserves, at the very least, the Padma Bhushan... In a border state like this (West Bengal), Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said.Kumar, who became an Election Commissioner in 2024 and CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced allegations from the Opposition that he has “favoured” the BJP.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Students strike across Germany against military service
articles.summary: A law establishing voluntary military service came into effect in January, but protest organisers fear compulsory service could follow.
articles.body:
School strikes are taking place across Germany to protest against the possible reintroduction of compulsory military service.

One of the organisers of the strike, Bela Breitner, from School Strike Against Compulsory Military Service said the federal government was "serious about gradually reintroducing compulsory military service".

At one protest in Hamburg, demonstrators waved flags and held up banners emblazoned with the words "We won't take part in your wars".

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has made boosting Germany's military a priority following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

A new law introducing voluntary military service came into force in January , with the aim of recruiting volunteers to increase the number of soldiers.

However, if the security situation worsens or if too few volunteers come forward, a form of compulsory military service could be considered by Germany's Parliament, the Bundestag.

Under the law, all 18-year-olds in Germany are being sent a questionnaire asking if they are interested and willing to join the armed forces.

One protester, 16-year-old Elias Bernhard, from Hamburg, said that the responses to the questionnaires "show that young people do not want to join the Bundeswehr [Germany's armed forces]".

"That is why I am out on the streets today. That is why we are serious about striking until compulsory military service is off the table. We will carry on."

The questionnaire is mandatory for men and voluntary for women. All 18-year-old men will have to take a medical exam to assess their fitness for possible military service.

The organisers of the protests, say the trigger came after some 18-year-olds in the northern German towns of Kiel and Flensburg, were sent official invitations for medical exams, even though they expressed no interest in joining the army on their registration forms.

The group says over a hundred demonstrations are planned across Germany, including in Kiel, Hamburg, Berlin and Frankfurt.

A spokesperson for the Defence Ministry told the BBC that under the law, the obligation to undergo a medical examination applies "to all men liable for military service who were born after 31 December 2007".

This also applies to people who have stated that they have no interest in compulsory military service. The spokesperson said that since July around 1,000 18-year-old men, who showed no interest in the army, have had the medical exam.

During the Cold War, Germany, like many other European countries, had a large army. But it reduced its armed forces during the 1990s after the fall of the Iron Curtain.

Germany's former Chancellor, Angela Merkel, ended compulsory military service in 2011.

But now, in the face of perceived threats from Russia and heavy pressure from Germany's traditional ally, the US, Merz has vowed to transform the Bundeswehr into Europe's strongest conventional army.

The Bundeswehr currently has around 186,700 troops. By the early 2030s, Germany wants to raise the number to 260,000, supplemented by around 200,000 reservists, in order to meet new Nato force targets and strengthen Germany's defences.

articles.title: America laughs as Trump pivots from 'Kung Flu' to hug Xi’s panda diplomacy
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington DC to negotiate trade, technology, tariffs and the future of the
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington DC to negotiate trade, technology, tariffs and the future of the global economy. Instead, he got the most elaborate housewarming party ever thrown by a man desperate to impress his guest.A gobsmacked America is cracking up at US President Donald Trump’s over-the-top reception for Xi, with folks wondering “where Kung flu” -- a reference to the MAGA supremo’s needling nickname for Covid, for which he has long blamed China.One commentator compared Trump's welcome of Xi to a nine-year-old showing off his bedroom -- with legos, video games and bunk beds -- to a friend, before transferring the analogy to the White House, where the US President showed off his gilded Oval office, his presidential hall of fame, and a helipad -- which one wag noted the Chinese would have built in two days, if not two hours.Another joked that Trump sounded like “a Long Island mom trying to set her adult daughter up on a date.” A third transformed Trump’s airport welcome of Xi into an imaginary presidential ride-sharing service called “Uber Trump.” The joke: Why summon an ordinary driver when the president himself can pick you up?Not known for fawning over any one, astonished American commentators wondered if Trump had offered Xi a pair of slippers for a sleepover at the White House, thrown rose petals at the foot of his bed, and asked him whether he wanted the guest Wi-Fi password.As it turned out, Xi kept his distance, staying at the Waldorf Astoria, a few blocks from the White House, and not even at Blair House, which is right opposite the White House and typically hosts state guests. Aside: Xi stayed at Blair House during his 2015 visit; and the property that is now Waldorf Astoria was formerly a Trump hotel.The comedy began even before Xi had reached the ceremonial reception, with the image of Trump wincing at the noise from US bombers launching a thousand quips. “Trump picked him up at the airport? That is friendship. I don’t even pick my own kid up at the airport!” gagged Desi Lydic on the Daily Show, joking that Trump recoiling at the roar of a US bomber flying overhead was like a child startled by the noise of its own fart. "For a man who's always screaming about China, Hairman Mao laid it on very thick today,” joked Jimmy Kimmel.There was also food. Fallon contrasted the elegant Chinese-influenced dishes at the dinner banquet with Trump’s preferred “two Big Mac with large fries and a diet coke,” while Kimmel warned that China sending pandas to the US was a bad idea because Trump may just eat them. "I'm not saying Trump is sucking up to him, but the Kennedy Center is now called the Xi Kennedy Center," Fallon quipped.Across both late-night stages and social media, the jokes clustered around the same themes: the extravagant, almost childlike eagerness of the reception (airport pickup, red carpets, renovation tours, helipad pride); the contrast with Trump’s earlier hard-line China bluster; the superficiality of the pageantry versus unresolved issues; food contrasts (elegant Chinese-American fusion versus Trump’s fast-food preferences); and the panda gift as both charming and comically mismatched.The humor treated the summit less as high diplomacy and more as a high-production personal friendship performance, with Trump’s fawning providing the punchlines, including an observation from Seth Meyers that "not even Chinese citizens gush this much about Xi." The short trade-truce extension and absence of any major breakthroughs only sharpened the focus on the optics, offering plenty of fire for satire.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Discarded oyster shells from San Antonio restaurants and events are being recycled to rebuild oyster reefs in the Gulf of Mexico, improve water quality and create marine habitat
articles.summary: What happens to oyster shells after the meal is over?
articles.body: What happens to oyster shells after the meal is over? Along the Texas coast, discarded shells from restaurants, festivals and community events are being given a second life as building material for oyster reefs. The effort is helping support marine ecosystems while keeping thousands of oyster shells out of the waste stream.In San Antonio, the South Texas Coastal Initiative (STCI) is collecting oyster shells and sending them to Sink Your Shucks, an oyster shell recycling program operated by Texas A&M University and the Harte Research Institute in Corpus Christi. The recycled shells are then used to help restore oyster reefs in the Gulf of Mexico, providing habitat for marine life and helping improve water quality.Turning oyster waste into reef restorationThe scale of the effort becomes particularly clear during San Antonio’s Fiesta Oyster Bake. Organizers say residents consume about 100,000 oysters during the festival weekend alone, leaving behind a significant volume of shells that can be repurposed for oyster reef restoration.STCI says recycling those shells has become increasingly important because more oysters are harvested and consumed than remain in the water to reproduce and help sustain natural reefs.“We actually pick up all the shells at the Oyster Bake,” Ernest Brown of the South Texas Coastal Initiative told KSAT. “We give them to the Sink Your Shucks program ... and they use them to rebuild oyster reefs.”The process turns what would otherwise be discarded waste into a resource for coastal conservation.Why oyster reefs matterOyster reefs play an important role in the health of coastal ecosystems. They provide habitat for fish, shrimp, crabs and other marine species, while oysters themselves help filter the water around them.“One single oyster can filter 50 gallons of water, which is huge and very important for the ecosystem,” Jorge Rodriguez, an STCI supporter and member, said, according to KSAT.Brown compared oysters’ role in the marine environment to the way trees help clean the air.“First and foremost, (the goal is) to clean the water, get rid of the pollution, because that helps all the other fish and animals and shrimp and crabs,” Brown said. “They’re a real key species because of what they do to keep the environment clean. They’re like trees cleaning the air.”Restaurants are becoming part of the recycling effortThe oyster shell recycling program extends beyond major events. A company contracted by STCI collects oyster shells from San Antonio restaurants two to three times a week.The shells cannot simply be returned to the water immediately after collection. They must first be cleaned and prepared before being transported back to the Texas coast for use in reef restoration.That logistical effort comes with a significant annual cost. Brown said STCI needs to raise about $150,000 each year to support the program through fundraising efforts and online donations.H-E-B has also contributed to the initiative, donating $50,000 toward the oyster restoration effort.“We were really compelled by their passion behind what they do, which is ultimately to restore the oyster population in the Texas bays,” Lainey Riebesehl with H-E-B Environmental Affairs said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Singapore welcomes Southeast Asia’s first okapi calf: Why this rare ‘forest giraffe’ is so unusual
articles.summary: A rare okapi calf has been born at Rainforest Wild Adventure in Singapore, marking the first recorded birth of an okapi in Southeast Asia.
articles.body: A rare okapi calf has been born at Rainforest Wild Adventure in Singapore, marking the first recorded birth of an okapi in Southeast Asia. The male calf was born on July 27 to first-time parents Kisala, 7, and Xandor, 4, at Mandai Wildlife Group’s wildlife park.The calf weighed about 20kg when it was first weighed a day after birth. Nearly two months later, it has more than doubled its weight to 48kg. The young okapi is being cared for with its mother in the Hidden Forest at Rainforest Wild Adventure East.Okapis are an endangered species and are rarely seen even in zoos. Native only to the dense rainforests of the Democratic Republic of Congo, the animals are listed as Endangered on the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List. Habitat loss and poaching have contributed to a sharp decline in their wild population.What is an okapi?Despite its zebra-like striped legs and brown body, the okapi is actually the closest living relative of the giraffe. It shares several characteristics with giraffes, including a long, flexible tongue and bony, horn-like structures called ossicones on the head of males.The animal is sometimes described as a “forest giraffe” because it lives in dense tropical forests rather than the open grasslands associated with giraffes. Its striped hindquarters and legs are thought to provide camouflage in the forest undergrowth.Okapis are elusive, largely solitary animals that live in the forests of northeastern and central Democratic Republic of Congo. Their habitat provides dense vegetation in which they can browse for leaves, shoots and other plant material.Why okapi calves are unusualThe Singapore calf has also been displaying a behaviour that may seem surprising to visitors. Instead of constantly following its mother, the young okapi spends much of its time hidden in its den, reports said.This is normal for the species. Okapi calves naturally remain concealed for much of their first few months, while their mothers leave them periodically to forage and return to nurse them. This behaviour is believed to help protect the young from predators.Okapis also have an unusually long pregnancy. Gestation lasts around 14 to 15 months — roughly 440 days — and females generally give birth to a single calf.Mandai said it prepared a quiet, secluded calving box for Kisala and her calf to allow them to follow this natural behaviour. The calf has recently been given access to its outdoor habitat, although keepers said it is still taking time to become comfortable in the new surroundings.A first for Southeast AsiaKisala and Xandor arrived in Singapore under the EAZA Ex situ Programme, a coordinated breeding programme for threatened species. The programme works to maintain healthy populations of endangered animals under human care, including through managed breeding and the movement of animals between participating institutions.Visitors to Rainforest Wild Adventure East can see Kisala and the calf in the Hidden Forest, although the youngster may retreat to its den. A live “baby monitor” also allows visitors to catch glimpses of the calf when it is inside.Mandai has invited the public to help choose the calf's name. The three options are Imara, meaning “strong” in Swahili; Mayaka, meaning “pearl” in Lingala; and Kiah, meaning “dawn”, “new beginnings” or “start of the season” in Swahili.You use AI every day. articles.title: I'm not tempted to call an early election, Andy Burnham says
articles.summary: The prime minister told the BBC an early poll would throw the country into a "backward-looking process".
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has insisted he is not tempted to call an early general election, arguing it would throw "the country into a backward-looking process".

During a round of BBC interviews ahead of Labour's annual conference, the prime minister said his focus was on helping people with the cost of living and supporting businesses.

Recent polling has suggested Labour's position has improved since Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer in Downing Street in July, although Reform UK and the Conservatives are not far behind.

An early general election could give Burnham a mandate of his own and free him from commitments made in Labour's 2024 manifesto. The next general election must be held by August 2029.

Asked by ITV Calendar if the next election would be in 2029, he replied: "Yes, that's when the next election will be.

"All of this speculation on an early election, I can knock that dead."

New policies, election speculation: What to expect from Burnham's first Labour conference as PM

Burnham heads to his first Labour Party conference as prime minister this weekend, with speculation over the prospect of a snap election likely to be a topic of conversation among some of those attending the event in Liverpool.

Labour has been projected to lose its majority but remain the largest party in the House of Commons if there was a snap election, according to recent polling.

It comes amid media reports that some of the prime minister's advisers have been weighing up the prospect of an election as early as next year.

But Burnham sought to rule out this prospect during interviews with BBC regional political editors ahead of the conference opening on Sunday.

Asked by BBC West political editor Paul Barltrop whether he was tempted to call an early poll, Burnham replied: "No, not particularly. No, I'm not.

"I see all the speculation and it just races ahead," he said.

He added: "No election anytime soon. I'm focused on the job as prime minister, doing what I said I would do."

He was later asked by BBC East Midlands political editor Peter Saull if there would be a general election next May, alongside council elections in the area.

The PM replied "no" before adding: "Not having a general election."

Burnham also said he wants to use the conference to say more about "the direction I want to take the country in", adding: "The focus is on that, helping people with the cost of living, helping businesses with the cost of running a business.

"These have got to be the priorities right now, rather than throwing the country into a backward-looking process where we're arguing again amongst ourselves."

Burnham said he wanted to ensure people are "feeling a bit of hope in their lives again", adding: "That's what I'm trying to do, and I hope to take it further in the coming period, rather than putting people back into an election cycle."

The prime minister was also asked about the number of migrants crossing the English Channel in small boats.

It comes after 781 people were recorded arriving in 10 boats on Wednesday, the highest total for a single day so far this year.

Burnham said his goal was that he didn't "want to see any crossings at all".

He declined to put a timescale on the ambition, but said his government would "not stop" working until crossings went "right down".

He argued that Brexit had hampered the UK's ability to stop the arrivals, saying it had led to a "loss of collaboration with neighbours".

Elsewhere in the series of interviews, he said:

He would not do any "special interviews" with The Sun. In 2015, he told the BBC he had not forgiven the newspaper for its coverage of the 1989 Hillsborough disaster.

Tourists would not "begrudge paying a few extra pounds" as a result of his proposal to allow regional mayors in England to charge new tax on visitors' overnight stays

The government would "do what we can within the resources that we've got to support people" in the Budget next month

articles.title: Wales' first national football museum to open in Wrexham
articles.summary: The Football Museum of Wales and Wrexham Museum is the first of its kind.
articles.body:
A museum showcasing the history of football in Wales is set to open to the public.

The Football Museum of Wales and Wrexham Museum is the first of its kind, and will bring to life artefacts and memorabilia spanning 150 years of the beautiful game in Wales.

Following a major redevelopment, part of the museum has also been designated to the history of Wrexham, showing how people lived and worked in the city over centuries.

About 70% of the football material on display will not have been exhibited before.

Curator Nick Jones highlighted five artefacts to see when visiting.

Wales first played in the World Cup in 1958, and their star player, John Charles, was playing for Juventus in Italy.

Picking players to play for Wales wasn't as easy as it is now, with Juventus apparently reluctant to release Charles because Italy hadn't qualified.

Eventually, however, Italy allowed the "Gentle Giant" from Swansea to represent his country.

The telegram, which would now be an email, shows Italian counterparts giving permission for Charles to play just a few days before the first match following what the Italians described as "difficulties and exigencies".

One of the museum's most prized possessions is William Harrison's cap from 1899 .

Harrison played a couple of international matches for Wales, and also played for Wrexham.

It was given to the museum in 2021 following the family of Stoke City striker Walter Watkins donating his Wales international cap from 1905 , having spent decades in Australia, believing it to be Wales' oldest.

Paul Swainson, Harrison's great-grandson, donated the cap a week after Watkins family gave theirs.

Harrison's cap is similar to Watkins', but has black stitching rather than the gold braiding that later became common.

Eddie May's 1977-78 shirt is a "special possession", said Jones.

The former footballer's shirt was donated by his son, Paul.

May played and managed all the major Welsh clubs, making more than 300 appearances for Wrexham and 90 for Swansea, as well as managing Cardiff and Newport.

Jones said: "It's a nice shirt and story, and we decided to put it on for the Swansea section."

Pennants are often exchanged at the start of football matches, and there are more than 20 on display

One of the "most special" is from when Wales faced Portugal in Lisbon on 15 May 1949.

Tommy "TG" Jones exchanged pennants with Francisco Ferreira.

It's one of the oldest in the collection, and has been restored before going on display.

"It was in quite poor condition before and thread bare at the bottom, but it's all been repaired. It's back to it's former glory," said Jones.

A football that still harbours a mystery of when it was actually made.

Tom Hughes was a saddler from Llangollen and made balls for the Football Association of Wales (FAW) in the 20th Century.

This particular ball was "quite mouldy" when it was donated, but has now been restored.

Nobody knows when the ball was made, but the label says it was played in a Wales v England international.

The museum believe it was used in the 1920s after World War One, but research indicates it could be even older than that.

The Football Museum of Wales and Wrexham Museum opened to the public on Friday.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to use controversial database to check voter citizenship
articles.summary: Critics have questioned the reliability of the data, warning it could  result in US citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls.
articles.body:
The US Supreme Court has lifted restrictions on the Trump administration to use a controversial federal database that uses citizenship information and other sensitive data to identify voters suspected of being non-citizens.

Critics have questioned the reliability of the data, warning it could result in US citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls.

In June, a federal judge ruled that the system was illegal and violated the privacy rights of Americans.

But the top court's conservative majority ruled that the National Voter Registration Act prohibits broad purges of voter rolls in the weeks before an election, which limits any "potential impact" of the decision ahead of the midterms.

But states can still check the citizenship of individual voters.

The three liberal-leaning justices on the Supreme Court dissented from the majority decision.

One of the dissenting Supreme Court justices, Ketanji Brown Jackson, expressed concern that this could mistakenly revoke the voting rights of eligible voters.

"The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the non-existent harm that the government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take," she wrote.

The Department of Homeland Security programme, known as Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (Save), allows officials to verify the eligibility of voters on their rolls.

The database was first created in 1986 to help officials verify the citizenship or immigration status of those applying for public benefits.

But the Trump administration last year expanded its search capabilities by allowing bulk searches using sensitive information from Social Security rolls.

In June, however, US District Judge Sparkle L Soonnan - a Biden-appointee - ruled that the revamped system shows that the federal government "knowingly trampled on the privacy rights" of US citizens "in a manner that threatens the sacred right to vote".

A federal appeals court allowed her ruling to stand, only to be overridden by the Supreme Court on Friday.

The top court ruled that a 1996 law allows DHS to seek citizenship and immigration data from federal agencies, and has "an obligation to respond" to states seeking that information.

The use of the Save programme by individual states is voluntary.

The previous judge's order, the Supreme Court ruled, "prevents the federal government from using the programme it believes is best suited to the task".

Voting rights groups called the ruling "profoundly disappointing".

"...it puts millions of Americans at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration's unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections," the League of Women Voters, the lead plaintiff in the case, said in a statement.

"We will be doing everything in our power to protect Americans' voting and privacy rights by ensuring that the district court decision stands," it said.

Lawyers for the Trump administration have long argued that the system is lawful and necessary to prevent non-citizens from voting. A total of 27 states currently use the system to check voter citizenship.

Critics, however, have pointed to a number of cases of the system already having led to mistakes.

For example, officials in Travis County, Texas, found that of nearly 100 voters identified as non-citizens, at least 10% of them - and potentially more - were US citizens, according to US media reports.

Since the state began checking its voter rolls with the Save system last year, only three non-citizen voters have been charged with illegally voting in Texas.

Since returning to the White House in January last year, the Trump administration has sought to reform the US electoral system, a process that has included a bid - rejected by the Supreme Court - to reign in mail-in ballots.

In 2024, for example, Texas Governor Greg Abbott announced that 1,930 people with a "voter history" had been removed from electoral rolls out of a total of nearly 18 million registered voters.

The figures are far below the hundreds of thousands of non-citizen voters that Trump and the Department of Homeland Security have previously suggested were on voter rolls.
